description: We are a group of young aspiring developers, and highschool students interested in computer science and astronautics.
summary: **Frontier Space Rocketeer** is an interactive 2D space mission simulator designed to make rocketry and space science more accessible and engaging for students. Players can explore the process of planning and carrying out space missions by configuring spacecraft and payloads and navigating missions while monitoring important flight information such as telemetry and trajectory. The project addresses the lack of accessible, hands-on learning resources by allowing students to experiment with spaceflight concepts rather than only reading about them or watching videos, which can be difficult for some people to learn from. It introduces ideas from physics, engineering, and orbital mechanics through interactive gameplay, helping players understand how different decisions affect mission outcomes and see them happen in real time, rather than just a hypothesis. This project is also important because early exposure to STEM through practical and engaging experiences can encourage curiosity, develop problem-solving skills, and inspire more young people to explore careers in aerospace and space science.
details:
Space Frontier Rocketeer is a browser-based educational mission simulator that lets students step into the shoes of aerospace engineers to plan, build, and pilot complete space missions from launch to splashdown. In the Vehicle Assembly Building, players design custom multi-stage rockets by selecting crew capsules or satellite payloads, fairings, fuel tanks, decouplers, engines, power and communication systems, and scientific instruments. Once on the launchpad, they navigate scaled environments, including Low Earth Orbit, Trans-Lunar Injection transfers, lunar landings, and atmospheric re-entry, while monitoring live telemetry, predicted orbital trajectories, and guidance from a Mission Control director.

Rather than relying on static textbook theory, the simulation turns abstract concepts in physics and orbital mechanics into an intuitive, hands-on experience where players immediately see how mass fractions, staging, and propulsion choices affect flight outcomes. By offering a zero-cost, exploratory platform that runs on standard desktop and laptop browsers without specialized hardware, the project aims to democratize rocketry and spark genuine student interest in STEM.

Under the hood, the application is built with vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, pairing custom procedural graphics on HTML5 Canvas 2D with real-time synthesized sound effects, such as engine roars, ambient space music, and button clicks via the Web Audio API. What makes the platform unique is how it unifies engineering design, mission planning, and real-time flight simulation into a single workstation that adapts to different skill levels through dual difficulty settings (Grades 6-8 vs. Grades 9-12) and toggleable Training or Expert flight-assist modes. To balance educational rigor with engaging gameplay, planetary models and physics parameters are grounded in verified NASA planetary data and launch vehicle archives, yet carefully scaled so a full orbital or lunar mission can be completed in five to ten minutes without sacrificing authentic engineering trade-offs.
